claims.statement: Hammersmith and Fulham Council projects a £160 million budget gap by the 2030-31 financial year.
claims.sourceQuote: Hammersmith and Fulham Council faces a projected £160 million budget deficit by 2030-31, driven by significant reductions in central government funding.
claims.sourceDocument: Full Council Hammersmith and Fulham, 21 October 2026

claims.statement: Relying purely on council tax increases to close the deficit would necessitate a 150% rise.
claims.sourceQuote: He revealed that if the council were to rely solely on council tax rises to bridge the gap, it would require an increase of 150%.
claims.sourceDocument: Full Council Hammersmith and Fulham, 21 October 2026

claims.statement: The council shared details on the financial situation with 94,000 local households.
claims.sourceQuote: Councillor Stephen Cowan, Leader of the Council, emphasised the council's commitment to financial efficiency and transparency, noting that detailed information had been communicated to 94,000 households.
claims.sourceDocument: Full Council Hammersmith and Fulham, 21 October 2026

takeawayCard.title: Council cuts back office costs
takeawayCard.subtitle: Services will be protected alongside green investment.

keyPoints: The council projects a £160 million shortfall by 2030 due to grant reductions.
Covering the deficit solely through council tax would require a 150% rise.
Leaders will cut back office functions while expanding a £5m green scheme.
